fields.features_heading: What Payroll Needs Before the First Deduction
fields.features_subheading: A signed sheet in a drawer leaves payroll guessing. Build a form that records the schedule and who signed it.
fields.feature_1:
Questions that follow the deduction type

The employee picks the deduction, such as a pay advance or parking, and the form asks only what that type needs. An advance asks for the total; parking asks for a start date.
fields.feature_2:
Every paycheck listed before signing

Enter the total and the amount per paycheck, and the form lists each deduction with its pay date. The employee reads the full schedule on the same screen where they sign.
fields.feature_3:
A signature from any phone

Employees sign with a finger on a phone or with a mouse at a desk. The app saves the signature next to the authorization text they saw. Payroll can pull up both of them later.
fields.feature_4:
Alerts that say a form is in, nothing more

Payroll gets an email or a Slack message that an authorization or a stop request has arrived, with a link. Amounts and names stay in the app instead of sitting in an inbox.
fields.feature_5:
Balances that count down each payday

Every active authorization shows what it takes each payday and the balance owed. When one paycheck's worth remains, the app marks the deduction final so payroll can end it.
fields.feature_6:
Code you can take to GitHub

On paid plans, export the full code to your GitHub repository and run the form beside your payroll system. Every signed authorization stays in a database that you own.

fields.usecase_heading: One Form for Every Deduction Staff Agree To
fields.tab_content_1:
Every $50 deduction listed before he signs

Jonah Koskivaara needed a $600 pay advance from Orrinvale Freight. He picks the advance on the form, and it lays out 12 deductions of $50, each with its payday. He reads the list, then signs. Payroll gets an email that says an authorization is in, with a link and no amounts.
fields.tab_content_2:
Her signature goes in before the kit order does

Imelda Ambrozetti orders a $240 tool kit through Brackenholt Mechanical's form on her phone, between two service calls. She picks 4 paychecks of $60. The submit button stays locked until she signs with her finger, and her signature is saved next to the exact wording she agreed to.
fields.tab_content_3:
In by Wednesday noon, off Friday's paycheck

Tess Okonski pays $25 a paycheck to park at Calloway Pike Grocers. After a move across town, she files a stop request on Tuesday. Any request in by Wednesday noon comes off that Friday's paycheck, and Friday is the first payday without her deduction. Payroll gets a Slack message that a stop request is in.
fields.tab_content_4:
With $45 left, this payday ends it

Winnowmere Dental's office manager keeps four deductions open on one screen, each with its amount per paycheck and the balance left. Cosmo Brede bought dental loupes at $45 a paycheck, and $45 is all that remains. The app marks his deduction final. This payday is his last one.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Payroll Deduction Form
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to build a payroll deduction authorization form template that shows the schedule before signing and tracks each balance.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Gather the deductions you take now
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Decide the schedule for each type
fields.howto_step_1_des: List every deduction you take today that needs the employee's consent, such as pay advances, uniforms, tools, and parking. Each one becomes a choice at the top of the form. A trucking yard and a dental office end up with different lists.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Write the authorization text in plain sentences: what is deducted, how much per paycheck, for how long, and how the employee can ask to stop it. Have your payroll provider or employment counsel review the wording before anyone signs it.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Decide how each type is paid back. An advance needs a total and an amount per paycheck, while parking runs until the employee stops it. The form uses these answers to list every paycheck deduction on the signing screen.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Describe the form in a prompt, naming each deduction type with its questions and saying where the signature step goes. Emergent builds it with the database table behind it, and you change any part of it by prompting again.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Choose who hears about each form
fields.howto_step_5_des: Choose who is told when a signed form or a stop request comes in, by email or in Slack. Keep amounts and names out of the message. A link back to the app is all payroll needs to open the record.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Test it with a made-up advance, a tool kit order, and a stop request filed just before the cutoff. Check that each schedule adds up to its total and that each alert carries only the link. Delete the test records before launch.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Publish the form where staff sign
fields.howto_step_7_des: Publish the form on its own link or on a custom domain (built into Emergent, uses credits). Employees fill it out on a phone or at a desk, and every signed authorization lands in a database you own, ready for payroll on the next pay run.

faq_plan.q: What is a payroll deduction authorization form template?
faq_plan.a: A payroll deduction authorization form template is a reusable form an employee signs to agree that a set amount comes out of their pay. It names the deduction, the amount per paycheck, and how many paychecks it runs. The employee signs and dates it.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a payroll deduction authorization form template?
faq_plan.a: Tell Emergent's AI form builder which deductions you offer and what each one asks, and put a signature step at the end. Emergent builds the form and the database behind it. Then run a few made-up employees through it before launch.

faq_plan.q: Which fields does a payroll deduction authorization form template need?
faq_plan.a: Include the employee's name and ID, the deduction type, the total, the amount per paycheck, the start date, and the number of paychecks. Add the authorization wording, how to ask to stop the deduction, and a signature with the date.

faq_plan.q: Can a payroll deduction authorization form template include a way to stop the deduction?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Add a stop request that names the deduction, and payroll ends it from a set paycheck. Put the request in the same app with a cutoff, such as Wednesday noon for Friday's paycheck. A change in pay rate or hours belongs on a payroll change form instead.

faq_plan.q: Can employees sign a payroll deduction authorization form template on a phone?
faq_plan.a: Yes. An app built with Emergent can capture an e-signature on a phone or a desktop and keep it with the wording the employee saw. Ask your employment counsel whether an electronic signature meets the rules that apply to your deductions.

faq_plan.q: How does a payroll deduction authorization form template handle required tools?
faq_plan.a: Within a federal limit. 29 CFR 531.35 covers tools of the trade that the employer requires. It names a violation in any workweek when the cost of such tools purchased by the employee cuts into the minimum or overtime wages required to be paid. Have payroll check each tool schedule against that limit.

faq_plan.q: What deductions can one payroll deduction authorization form template cover?
faq_plan.a: One form can cover pay advances, uniforms, tools, parking, and other voluntary deductions, with each type asking its own questions. Keep each signed authorization to a single deduction so it can end on its own. When a customer pays by card instead of through payroll, a credit card authorization form does that job.

faq_plan.q: How long should records from a payroll deduction authorization form template be kept?
faq_plan.a: At least 2 years under the federal rule. 29 CFR 516.6 covers Records of additions to or deductions from wages paid, and says employers shall preserve for a period of at least 2 years. Confirm your own period with counsel. The app keeps every signed form in a database you own.

faq_plan.q: How does a payroll deduction authorization form template show the repayment schedule?
faq_plan.a: It divides the balance by the amount taken each payday and turns the result into a dated list of paychecks. A $360 balance at $40 a paycheck becomes 9 deductions. The employee scrolls that list on the screen where they sign.

faq_plan.q: Who should review a payroll deduction authorization form template before use?
faq_plan.a: A payroll specialist or an employment attorney, before the first employee signs. Send them the wording and one sample schedule. When they ask for edits, prompt Emergent with the new wording, and the form shows it to every employee who signs after that.

plan.angle: The top 10 is blank paper: Word and PDF downloads, a university and a state agency PDF, an HR association sample, and a six-template pack (loan, uniform, one-time). Each is a box for an amount and a signature line. This page is for the payroll or HR lead who builds the authorization as a working form: the employee picks the deduction type, sees the per-paycheck amount and the number of paychecks before signing, signs on a phone, can ask to stop a deduction, and payroll sees every active authorization and its remaining balance in a database the employer owns. Alerts carry no pay details, only that a form is in and a link.
